From axioms of finite projective planes q≥2, all ordered triples have universal depth-one extension profiles: one all-equal, nine exactly-two-equal, two distinct same-side collinear/concurrent versus nonconcurrent, twelve mixed types. For mixed triples the relevant zero-witness counts include q(q−1)−1≥1, and singleton masks exist for q−1≥1, including q=2. These 24 profiles imply four universal depth-two pair types, then a single depth-three vertex type, hence the same depth-four root type by Ehrenfeucht–Fraïssé semantics. Independently implemented exact rank-profile comparison on PG(2,2) and PG(2,3): uncolored rank4 equal; named-sort rank3 equal and rank4 different. Rank5 uncolored separation has explicit ∃vertex with four distinct neighbors (degrees 3 vs4). Named-sort rank4 sentence chooses three concurrent lines and point off their union, q(q−2)>0 iff q≥3; conjunction of independent point-existential and off-point existential keeps nesting depth four. Finite test not used to infer all-plane universality.
